hypotheses.persona: Family with a young child (toddler/preschooler) who attends daycare on weekdays but is at home on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.
hypotheses.rationale: The sippy cup at table on Sunday (17:47) confirms the child is present for dinner on the weekend. The cushion at sofa (13:13) suggests family relaxation. The phone at counter (08:59) and floor lamp at sofa (09:33, 10:12) are generic but fit a weekend morning. The waste bin at counter (10:53) and fork at table (11:39) are mundane. The doormat pattern (not seen on Fri, Sat, Sun) supports the child being at home all weekend. The child's presence on all three weekend days and the absence of doormat movements strongly suggest full-time care with daycare on weekdays.

hypotheses.persona: Single adult with a child visiting part-time (e.g., every other weekend or weekdays).
hypotheses.rationale: The child items appear on multiple days (Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday), but the doormat pattern (not seen on Friday, Saturday, Sunday) could still fit a part-time schedule. However, the sippy cup at table on Sunday (17:47) and the cushion at sofa (13:13) suggest the child is present for a full weekend, which is less typical for part-time care unless the adult works from home. The frequency of child items makes this less likely than full-time care.

The sippy cup, board book, diaper caddy, cushion, and playmat are very strong indicators of a child. The new evidence (sippy cup at table on Sunday) further contradicts this hypothesis. Only kept for completeness.
